overview.text: An imam is a Muslim leader, but the title has different meanings across traditions. In congregational worship, an imam leads ritual prayer; more broadly, it can describe a community leader recognized for religious learning. In Shi‘i Islam, “Imam” also names a distinct succession of leaders from Muhammad’s family, believed to have inherited religious and community leadership after his death. Twelver Shi‘a Muslims hold that there are twelve such Imams, beginning with Ali, and regard their leadership as divinely appointed. These meanings are connected by the idea of guidance, but an imam leading a mosque prayer is not automatically one of the Twelve Imams.

key_facts.text: “Imam” means “leader”; it commonly refers to the person leading daily ritual prayer.
The title can also describe a community leader whose role draws on religious learning.
In Shi‘i belief, an Imam is a divinely appointed successor to Muhammad from his family.
Twelver Shi‘a Muslims believe in twelve Imams, beginning with Ali.
The textbook describes Shi‘i Imams as non-prophets whose role includes protecting Muhammad’s teachings and interpreting scripture.
